---
title: "Case-report specification and export"
subtitle: "T.2 · after the postrank theory book, chapter 21, and the reading/exporting vignette"
description: "Reports accompanied by target definitions, computation scope, error-budget checks and source information."
---

The tool builds a grade report from the released probabilities for each case. The budget applies to the report
on the screen. The reporting view records the outcome, model assumptions, and search used to produce the grades.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/report-designer.js"></script>
<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["report-designer"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **CDE: three-grade family.** The browser enumerates all 523,251 capped reports. The chosen report states
  45 pairs. The result applies to the twelve schools in the teaching subset.
- **KRW: equal weights.** The result is labeled “optimal within this order” and states 636 pairs. Changing the weight
  can change the order and which reports the search considers. The supplied intervals describe race and gender separately.
- **Alabama: equal weights.** The report states 1,249 pairs. Grade 1 indicates favorable historical outcomes,
  including lower incarceration. The case and its text download give the population and interval level.
- **CDE: cap two.** The family contains 4,095 reports. Compare its best report with the archived report at the same withholding cost.
- **CDE: mean-order cap four.** The computation switches to the posterior-mean order. It is optimal only among
  cuts of that order. The budget table gives the difference between the allowed and expected error counts.
- **CDE: all withheld.** E/N reads NA: no disclosure. A homogeneous budget passes without stating anything,
  so a pass alone does not establish useful or error-free disclosure.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The archived status, bound, and gap apply to the archived computation. The current search has its own scope.
A shared grade leaves the comparison unstated. The expected error share describes individual comparisons in
aggregate, and the probability that every stated comparison is correct requires a joint calculation. A decision
to allocate resources would require a further rule. Draft text stays in the open component's memory.

CDE uses the fitted statewide prior. KRW uses historical contact-gap estimates from
[Kline, Rose and Walters](https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20230700) and their
[data deposit](https://doi.org/10.3886/E198284V1), under the deposit's CC-BY-NC terms (no version stated). The experiment describes historical contact gaps.
Alabama uses [Opportunity Atlas](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/NKCQM1) historical outcomes under CC BY 4.0.
The case notes and downloads give the source, changes, rights, and conditioning. These details appear on each CSV row.
Relations use `1` for row above column,
`-1` for column above row, `0` for withheld, and `NA` on the diagonal.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
The mean-order cap-four result states 54 pairs, with risk .0368858. With postrank 1.1.0 loaded:

```r
x <- pr_case_cde$input; s <- postrank_settings(weights = c(negative_chronic_absence = 1), tau = .2, G_max = 4)
a <- postrank_cuts(x$summaries$means[, 1], x, s, direction = "descending", rule = "optimal")
a$evaluation[c("N", "E_over_N", "primary_risk")]
```
:::
